newsitem.title: USA: No bail for U.S. lap-dance fan accused of murder.
newsitem.headline: No bail for U.S. lap-dance fan accused of murder.

text.p: Attorneys for latex glove salesman Craig Rabinowitz, accused of strangling his wife after squandering thousands of dollars in an obsession with an exotic dancer, withdrew their request that he be granted bail on Thursday.
The lawyers denied that an apparent suicide note from Rabinowitz revealed in media reports late on Wednesday was a factor in the decision to withdraw the bail request.
But they said they had taken steps to obtain a psychiatric evaluation of their client, and were investigating alternative explanations for the killing.

"We need more time to do things -- run down leads which we're working on, and we need more time to refute some of the allegations the district attorney has made," attorney Jeffrey Miller told reporters after the withdrawal was granted in a brief court hearing.
Also on Thursday, the lead prosecutor in the case said he was looking into the possibility that Rabinowitz took money from investors in a business that does not appear to exist.

Rabinowitz was not present for the hearing, but appeared before Montgomery County Court of Common Pleas Judge Samuel Salus in a closed-door session to confirm his acceptance of the withdrawal. The request can be reinstated in the future.
Rabinowitz, 33, was accused of killing his wife Stephanie, 29, a part-time lawyer for a prestigious Philadelphia firm.
Police found Stephanie dead -- nude and still wearing jewelry -- in the bathtub of the couple's home in the prosperous Philadelphia suburb of Merion early on April 30.
Rabinowitz told police he heard a thump in the bathroom as his wife was bathing, then found her unresponsive about 20 minutes later, according to a police report.
A medical examiner concluded she was murdered by strangulation.
The couple had a year-old daughter.

Prosecutors alleged in court documents that Rabinowitz was heavily in debt and spent more than $35,000 in the previous three months on an exotic dancer, nicknamed "Summer," at Delilah's Den, an upscale strip club where patrons can obtain private "lap dancing" sessions for $100 per half hour.
They also alleged he pawned Stephanie's engagement ring a two days after her death.
He killed Stephanie to collect on a $1.5 million insurance policy on her life, Montgomery County assistant district attorney Bruce Castor told Reuters.

"Craig Rabinowitz had amassed so much debt that he could never hope to get out of it. He had a strong attraction to this stripper, Summer, and he had a wife who was worth a lot more dead than alive," Castor said.
Castor also said Rabinowitz received "large sums" of money from potential investors, but there were no signs he was involved in any legitimate business. He said charges could be filed for theft.

The defence attorneys declined to discuss reports that a note from Rabinowitz indicating possible suicidal aims was found in his home on the day of his arrest, May 5. But attorney Frank DeSimone said "the suicide note in my opinion had nothing to do" with the decision to withdraw the bail request.
